brief.t: As of 2026-11-06, old-crop (2026/27) unfixed call **sales** are 68.2k contracts (-1,807 w/w, -4,380 over 8 weeks) and old-crop unfixed **purchases** 28.3k (+46 w/w). Against the same week of the last five seasons, sales are at the 73rd percentile (avg 72.4k) and purchases at the 47th (avg 33.8k). Beyond this season, merchants hold 12.0k of new-crop sales and 40.1k of new-crop purchases.

Net old-crop on-call is +39,899 (mill side). In old-crop COT, producers/merchants/processors/users hold 98.4k long and 205.5k short (net -107,066, +6,811 w/w). Their long/short ratio of 0.48 sits at the 23rd percentile of the last three years: **commercials hold relatively little long cover, so fixing the mill-side book is more likely to need buying in the market**. The net and the ratio matter more than gross longs, which include calendar-spread legs held by trade houses. On the other side, total unfixed purchases of 68.4k (+4,603 over 8 weeks) compare with 228.5k PMU shorts and 24.4k swap-dealer shorts — producer fixing is latent selling, whether it runs through PMU hedges or swap structures.

Front contract **December 2026** is 2.6 weeks from first notice, with 7.6k unfixed sales and 14.3k unfixed purchases against 111.8k open interest. Next: March 2027 with 30.5k unfixed sales. The Dec/Mar spread is -3.94¢, -0.10¢ on the week.

Old-crop unfixed sales of 7.11m bales equal 16% of USDA's 2026/27 world trade forecast (44.8m, November 2026). USDA sees Brazil exporting 16.0m bales vs the US 12.3m. US export sales (week of 2026-10-29): 4.39m running bales unshipped, China 7%.

Managed money is net long 53.1k (-3,042 w/w; 3-yr COT index 71). Spec length is elevated; with commercials light on long cover, mill fixing could still add buying, but a long spec book can also liquidate.
